top_level_note: US-market air-cooled Type 1 Beetle: sedan 1949-1977, Super Beetle sedan 1971-1975, convertible 1949-1979 (Super Beetle-based from 1971). The water-cooled, front-engine New Beetle (1998+) is a different car and is left out. Engines sold only outside the US (1200 after 1965, 1300 after 1966, Mexican/Brazilian Beetles) are not listed, even where Hagerty lists them.

excluded.why: not US models; CG: "1200 and 1300 engines continue outside U.S." from 1967

excluded.what: Engine code letters other than AJ (e.g. D, F, H, B, AE, AH, AK)
excluded.why: no reachable reputable source stated them (the Bentley, Chilton and Clymer manuals on the Internet Archive are lending-restricted); rpo gives the size instead

search_notes: No NHRA data (nhra=false throughout). Sources: VW factory literature on the Internet Archive (US owner's manuals 1962-1979, 1968/1969/1976 US brochures, 1952-57 and 1961-65 workshop manuals, the 1966 Canadian brochure and a 1979 Volkswagenwerk report to NHTSA), all counted as ONE source; the Krause Standard Catalog of Volkswagen (full-text search snippets only; the book is lending-restricted and snippets carry no year label, so years come from narrative and price-guide lines plus the bore/compression match); Consumer Guide via archived HowStuffWorks pages; the appendix of Nelson's Small Wonder (Bentley edition; the chart may derive from a VW of America booklet, but it is published as Nelson's book); Hagerty valuation pages (Wayback; non-US engines they list were ignored); Autobook 1954-67 (UK). Wikipedia gives only DIN figures and backs displacements. The Standard Catalog of Imported Cars snippets were unusable; no VW pages were found on oldcarbrochures; Hemmings is blocked. hp = what US literature states for that year: SAE gross through 1972, SAE net from 1973. DIN figures are in hp_din where a source states them.
